title: Beyond the Known: An Unknown-Aware Large Language Model for Open-Set Text Classification
claim: Closed-set methods rely on post-hoc detection over overlapping representations; conditioning on label subsets with an explicit unknown class separates OOD intrinsically.
layout: 3 columns, training over inference rows, left-to-right; shared legend on top
description: A wide figure with a dashed legend strip on top defining icons: input, ID label, OOD label, sub-label set, classifier heads. Below are three columns, (a) closed-set discriminative fine-tuning with a PLM, (b) closed-set generative fine-tuning with an LLM, and (c) open-set generative fine-tuning, which is the proposed method. Each column has a Training row on top and an Inference row below. Training rows show inputs flowing through the model to labels, with loss annotations. Column (c) adds sub-label-set boxes, the prompt text 'Given: sub label set ... Answer: OOD', and an OOD output. The inference rows show t-SNE scatter plots. Panels (a) and (b) show red OOD points overlapping ID clusters, with a 'Post-hoc OOD Detection' banner and a sad face. Panel (c) shows separated clusters and a happy face.
caption: Illustration of different fine-tuning methods. Representation visualizations show significant overlap between ID and OOD (red) in a) and b), whereas c) demonstrates clear separation.
abstract: Open-set text classification (OSTC) requires models to correctly classify in-distribution (ID) samples while reliably rejecting out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs—an essential capability for real-world NLP systems. Most OSTC methods train on ID data under the closed assumption that all outputs belong to the known label space and then perform OOD detection with the biased representations, which inherently lack awareness of unknowns and thus yield overconfident predictions on OOD inputs. In this work, we present UnLLM, an Unknown-aware Large Language Model for OSTC. Instead of fixing classification to the entire known label space, we reformulate it into a subset-conditioned text generation task: the LLM is prompted with sampled subsets of known labels, and any instance outside the candidate set is explicitly assigned as “unknown”. This reformulation transforms OOD detection from a post-hoc procedure into an intrinsic modeling capability. More importantly, our approach is the first to explicitly incorporate the unknown into classification, enabling systematic modeling of unknowns through a unified representation–logits–inference optimization, which progressively strengthens the model’s capacity to capture open-set risk. Extensive experiments across six benchmarks show that UnLLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines. Code and datasets are available at https://github.com/cx9941/UnLLM.
